methodology.scale: Shock-score scale. Six transmission channels (maritime denial, oil, US inflation impulse, Treasury stress, political stress, escalation risk), each 0–5, summed to 0–30. Bands: 0–7 watch · 8–14 stress · 15–21 systemic-risk watch · 22–30 crisis. Market channels move only on a confirmed close through a trigger, never on an intraday print — which is why the 26 August snapshot in this edition moves nothing. Maritime denial and escalation risk are event-based and move on events, not announcements: a declared posture, a stated objective, an issued-but-unimplemented framework or a trailed sanctions package is not an event. Hysteresis is asymmetric by design: a channel is upgraded on a sustained break of its trigger and downgraded only on a sustained reversal past a wider threshold. Two live illustrations this edition. The Treasury channel holds at 5 with its volatility leg satisfied for a sixth consecutive session and its yield leg at its narrowest since 28 July, because the rule requires sustained. And the US-inflation channel holds at 5 with its own firing trigger broken — the 5y5y forward closed below the 2.30% level that fired it — because the documented downgrade sits 15.71 bp lower at the pre-war anchor. That gap between the firing level and the downgrade level is reported rather than closed, and the rule is not moved to match the tape.
methodology.scaleCap: The saturated scale. FIVE of the six channels are at 5; only oil, at 2, is not — three points below the cap, not one. Deterioration cannot raise this score through any of the five, and the sole remaining route up is the oil channel, so a flat score is an artifact of the scale rather than a statement about stability. This edition is a fifth variant of the problem and a new one: the two records moved in opposite directions on the SAME subject. The diplomatic record improved materially — a written framework naming a corridor and a demining project, a live Pakistani channel, three Gulf capitals pushing publicly toward de-escalation, twenty-six nights with no strike inside Iran, a 28-day CENTCOM combat silence. The physical record deteriorated at the same time and on the same waterway: one cargo vessel and no tankers on the UKMTO annex for 24 August, Kpler’s thinnest day since early May, Windward recording no outbound transit at all, and the cumulative incident count moving from 94 to 96. The total registered neither. Readers should attend to the composition and to the distance-to-trigger figures, which are reported in basis points and dollars precisely so that movement inside a frozen total remains visible.

methodology.intraday: Intraday caveat, and a note on the section references. Numbered references of the form §9.n in the PDF edition point to the monitor’s internal operating instructions and pitfalls register, which records every failure mode the process has hit since June and the rule adopted in response; they are not sections of the published document. Two entries were added to that register by this edition. The first is that the visual render is not optional and a layout bug can masquerade as an over-length document: three text QA passes — 190 numeric checks and two adversarial prose passes returning 42 and then 30 defects — all ran clean on a build whose every table was rendering at a third of its width, and the bug presented as page pressure and drove real substance out of the edition before it was found. The second is that a fix is a new draft, and markup breaks silently: replacing a phrase that ended in a closing bold tag with text carrying its own opening tag produced a nested tag that killed the renderer, and a separate edit dropped a closing quote, so tag counts are now balance-checked and the document re-rendered after every edit round. On the data itself: the latest dated row is a Singapore-AM snapshot and US hours set the close; the error is regime-dependent rather than random and has ranged from thirteen cents to $3.99 on Brent within a fortnight. This edition’s reconciliation of the 21 August cut missed in BOTH directions at once — nominal yields understated by 3.38 to 5.48 bp while breakevens were overstated by about 2 bp — which makes it a real-yield session and is the opposite composition to the term-premium sessions that dominated the preceding fortnight. Series go dark for multiple sessions and backfill later, sometimes against the prevailing trend. A row can fail to refresh entirely, an individual field can carry forward inside an otherwise live row, and a continuation series can break silently across a contract roll. Every one of these failure modes has occurred since 29 July, each is tested for explicitly on every run, and the results of those tests are published rather than assumed.
